results.title: Querying GEO DataSets and GEO Profiles - NCBI - NIH
results.content:
| Field full name | Field aliases | Semantics | Allowed values and rules | Example |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Entry Type | `ETYP`, `entryType` | Record type | Fixed list: `gds` (DataSet), `gse` (Series), or `gpl` (Platform) | `gds[Entry Type]` — find only DataSet records |
| Organism | `ORGN`, `PORGN`, `primary organism` | Name of the organism | NCBI taxonomy terms; wildcard (`*`) supported. All levels in the taxonomy lineage and common names are indexed. | `Mus musculus[Organism]` — find studies performed on mouse |
| DataSet Type | `GTYP`, `gdsType` | DataSet or Series type | Fixed list; check the Advanced Search page for the list of indexed terms. | `expression profiling by high throughput sequencing[DataSet Type]` |
| Filter | `FILT`, `FLTR`, `SUBSET`, `SB`, `FIL` | Filters for records that have links to other NCBI databases | Fixed list; check the Advanced Search page for the list of indexed terms. | `gds pubmed[Filter]` — find records that have PubMed links |
| Title | `TITL`, `TITLE`, `TI` | Text from titles of DataSets, Series, Platforms, and Samples | Free text; wildcard (`*`) supported. | `Affymetrix[Title]` — find records where “Affymetrix” appears in a title |
| Description | `DESC`, `DSC`, `DESCR` | Text provided in the DataSet, Series, or Sample description, summary, and other metadata fields | Free text; wildcard (`*`) supported. | `smok*[DESC]` — find studies that contain smoking-related terms in their descriptions |
| Sample Source | `SRC`, `source` | Source of the biological material of the Sample; the page warns that this is a submitter-supplied field, not curated. | Free text; wildcard (`*`) supported. | `brain[Sample Source]` — find studies with samples from brain |
| Attribute | Not listed on the page | Not provided on the page. | Not provided on the page. | Not provided on the page. |
| Publication Date | `PDAT`, `DP` | Date on which the record was released | Format `YYYY/MM`; range function supported. | `2007/01:2007/06[Publication Date]` — find studies published between January and June 2007 |
| Update Date | `UDAT` | Date on which the record was last updated | Format `YYYY/MM`; range function supported. | `2010/06[Update Date]` — find records updated during June 2010 |
| Number of Samples | `NSAM`, `n_samples` | Number of Samples in the DataSet or Series | Integer; range function supported. | `100:500[Number of Samples]` — find studies with between 100 and 500 samples |
| Supplementary Files | `SFIL`, `SFILE`, `suppFile` | Supplementary file type names | Free text; wildcard (`*`) supported. | `cel[Supplementary Files]` — find studies that have Affymetrix CEL files |
| GEO Accession | `ACCN`, `accession` | GEO accession number | Valid DataSet (`GDS`), Platform (`GPL`), Sample (`GSM`), or Series (`GSE`) accession. | `GPL570[GEO Accession]` — find all studies performed on Platform GPL570 |

### Query syntax and construction

- General form: `term [field] OPERATOR term [field]`, where `term` is the search term and `field` is the search field.
- Boolean operators `AND`, `OR`, and `NOT` must be capitalized.
- Fields can be specified by their full name or an alias.
- Use quotes to search for a phrase:
  - `salt stress` retrieves studies mentioning both words anywhere in the description.
  - `"salt stress"` retrieves studies where the words occur as a phrase.
- Use parentheses to combine criteria as a unit:
  - `human[organism] AND (smok* OR diet)` retrieves human studies that mention either smoking or diet.
  - `human[organism] AND smok* OR diet` also returns studies mentioning diet regardless of organism.
- Use an asterisk (`*`) as a wildcard at the beginning or end of a text string, but not in the middle. For example, `smok*` retrieves documents containing words such as smoke, smoking, or smoker.
- Use a colon to specify a range, for example `2007/01:2007/06[Publication Date]`.
- The History section at the foot of Advanced Search pages can combine previous queries or find their intersection. Recent queries receive numbers that can be used in a search statement; examples include `#1 NOT #2` and `(#1 OR #2) AND human[organism]`.
results.description: Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) is a database repository of high throughput gene expression data and hybridization arrays, chips, microarrays.
